title: Religion
coreMove: Look at religious practice as belief plus visible loyalty, shared rhythm, and norm enforcement.
sourcePressure: The source frames religion as group bonding, loyalty display, and norm enforcement through sacrifice, ritual synchrony, badges, sermons, and supernatural enforcement.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer reduces religion to false belief or manipulative control and loses sincere bonding.

sourceAnchors.name: ritual synchrony
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says ritual synchrony helps groups bond.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Moving together can make belonging feel less like an opinion and more like a body fact.

sourceAnchors.name: badges and sermons
sourceAnchors.detail: The source names badges and sermons as visible tools of loyalty and norm enforcement.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The badge marks who stands inside; the sermon reminds everyone what standing inside requires.

sourceAnchors.name: supernatural enforcement
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says supernatural enforcement can matter for norm maintenance.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A watched norm does not need another person in the room to feel backed.

exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator seeing ritual as group support under stress
exampleSpecs.stakes: families need belonging and obligation made visible at bedside
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Eleanor watches the family sing the same quiet line and schedules chaplain coverage around shared practice rather than private belief alone.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Low singing reaches the nurses' station before the chart does.

exampleSpecs.audience: a leader distinguishing sacrifice from resume padding
exampleSpecs.stakes: visible hardship can bind the group and signal loyalty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Do we have to wear the shirts?" Vincent asks, and Petra explains the badge as a public promise to the group, not decoration.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Do we have to wear the shirts?" Vincent asks with the supply boxes still open.

exampleSpecs.audience: a director borrowing synchrony without belief claims
exampleSpecs.stakes: shared rhythm can enforce care norms even outside doctrine
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You have Hugo begin with one repeated note everyone can hold, turning scattered grief into a shared obligation to listen.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You hear the first note steady the room before anyone speaks.

exampleSpecs.audience: a treasurer using sermon norms to prevent factional spending
exampleSpecs.stakes: religious language can enforce group obligations around money
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aisha reads the benevolence rule aloud before the vote, making generosity a shared norm rather than one faction's preference.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The offering envelopes sit unopened beside the budget binder.

exampleSpecs.audience: a participant realizing cost makes commitment legible
exampleSpecs.stakes: sacrifice separates spectators from committed members
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Janek until the third blister to understand why the walk mattered: the cost made loyalty visible to himself and the group.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Janek until the third blister to reread the packing list.

exampleSpecs.audience: a moderator enforcing norms when no one shares a building
exampleSpecs.stakes: supernatural and social enforcement can overlap in digital practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Who keeps the promise when the camera turns off?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Who keeps the rule after the video tiles disappear?

skillTargets: identify loyalty display and norm enforcement in religious practice
explain ritual synchrony without dismissing belief
evaluate costly sacrifice as commitment signal

tryThisNowSpec: Watch one repeated group ritual, religious or not. Name the belief it expresses, the loyalty it displays, and the norm it reinforces.
